oracle-l5r-7991: The Compassion of the Unicorn: "As a Focus Effect: You may choose (now) to delay the effects of losing this duel until after the next Dynasty Phase begins. // Battle/Open: Choose your performing unbowed Unicorn Clan Personality and target another unit: Straighten it. Gain 1 Honor, or 2 Honor if you do not control the target." Unwired because of the Focus Effect only: it needs the shared delay mechanism Mendon and the coordinator are designing together ("delay effects / actions / a phase" -- Halls of the Forgotten, Strength of the Spider oracle-l5r-8362 and The Courage of the Mantis, oracle-l5r-7995, are blocked on the same clause). What is missing is a duel-loss consequence that is not applied when the duel resolves (Dueling.cs ApplyDuelOutcome applies the loser's consequences immediately) but is held, per duel and per loser, as a persisted pending consequence and released when the next Dynasty Phase begins (SetPhase(Phase.Dynasty) is the one place that phase starts), plus the "(now)" yes/no choice at Focus Effect resolution (FocusEffectChoice.cs is the place: a choice among {delay, do not delay}). The Battle/Open half is separately buildable from existing pieces: a performer category "own-unbowed-personality-with-keyword-at-battle" over the Unicorn Clan (a Clan check, HasClanAffiliation, like own-unbowed-spider-personality-at-battle), the "other-unit" target category, StraightenUnit, and GainHonor(1 or 2) read from whether the target is the player's own. It was not published half-built.
oracle-l5r-7995: The Courage of the Mantis: "As a Focus Effect: You may choose (now) to delay the effects of losing this duel until after the next Dynasty Phase begins. // Battle: If any enemy units are at the current battlefield, choose your performing unbowed Mantis Clan Personality: Move him there. You may take an additional Battle action." Unwired because of the Focus Effect only -- the same missing shared delay mechanism as The Compassion of the Unicorn (oracle-l5r-7991; see its note for what the mechanism must do). The Battle half is Broken Alliance's shape (Move: new(MoveSpec.Performer, MoveSpec.CurrentBattlefield), MovesToBattle, the enemy-units-at-the-battlefield Require) with a Mantis Clan performer (a Clan check) and GrantAdditionalAction(player.Id, null), and is buildable now. Not published half-built.
oracle-l5r-8137: The Honesty of the Phoenix: "As a Focus Effect: You may choose (now) to delay the effects of losing this duel until after the next Dynasty Phase begins. // Battle/Open: If you are a Phoenix Clan player, choose your performing unbowed Phoenix Clan Personality: Name a card. After the next resolution this turn of your action from another Strategy or Ring with that title, draw a card, and choose a player, who discards a card. Remove this card from the game." Three missing pieces: (1) the shared delay mechanism for the Focus Effect (see The Compassion of the Unicorn, oracle-l5r-7991); (2) NAMING a card title: there is no command or choice in the engine that names a title (a free-text or catalogue-list title choice on the acting player's command, validated against the catalogue), and (3) a standing per-turn watch keyed on the named title -- "after the next resolution this turn of your action from another Strategy or Ring with that title" -- which would read MatchState.LastResolvedAction (ActionEffectTracking.cs already records the resolved action's AbilityId/SourceId/PlayerId) once, then run a draw and a chosen player's discard (DeciderChoice.cs / ForcedDiscard cover the discard), and finally the cost "remove this card from the game" (CostVerbs.Remove exists and RemoveSource is declared). Only (1) and (2) are genuinely new structure; the watch is an AfterActionResolved-style watch like Fair Warning's.
oracle-l5r-7665: Surprise Attack: "Battle: Choose one or more of your performing Nonhuman Personalities at the current battlefield and target one of the enemy leader's Personalities there or at home: Create a battlefield (not associated with any province). Move all the performers and targets there." Blocked on the battlefield model: every battlefield in the engine IS one of the Defender's provinces (an index 0..3 -- UnresolvedBattlefields, CurrentBattleProvince (over 150 uses), Province.Reconnaissance, Province Strength and province destruction in ContinueResolveBattle, AdjacentProvinces, the Terrain and Region placement, the attack-assignment and battle-selection commands, and the client's per-province battle board via MatchView). A battlefield associated with no province needs a new battlefield concept (an id that is not a province index, with its own Terrain slot, Reconnaissance state, adjacency -- the printed text does not say whether it counts as adjacent to anything -- a resolution with no Province Strength and nothing to destroy, and a slot in the Attacker's battle order, since the core rules say every battlefield is fought exactly once), threaded through all of those readers and the client view. It could be built as a synthetic Province entry appended to the Defender's list flagged Phantom (Destroyed never set, Strength 0, excluded from Hidden Falls Dojo's and the maneuver assignment listings), but that touches every Provinces enumeration (the attack/defense assignment lists, DestroyProvince, victory checks) and the shared MatchView shape, and it is a larger change than one card justifies without Mendon's ruling on the open questions above (is the created battlefield fought as an extra battle this Attack Phase? which cards may be assigned or moved there? does it disappear when its battle ends?).
